title: Approximation Techniques in DI
tagline: Year 3 — Rounding before calculating: estimating growth, shares and ratios when the options are far apart

introduction.overview: In many DI questions the options are far apart and the question says "approximately". You do not need an exact answer; you need one that is close enough to choose the right option. Approximation saves time by rounding the data (4,180 to 4,200), simplifying ratios, using benchmarks (10% of a number is one tenth) and checking the size of the answer before doing the full arithmetic.
introduction.placementRelevance: Speed matters in DI sections of company tests, and approximation is the main way to gain time.
introduction.realWorldContext: Mental estimates of growth, shares and ratios are what managers do in meetings.

learningObjectives: Estimate growth, share and ratio quickly
Judge when approximation is safe from the option spacing

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: 10% of a number is the number divided by 10. 1% is divided by 100. A percentage change is change ÷ old.

coreDefinitions: Approximation: replacing a number by a nearby simpler one.
Benchmark: an easy fraction like 10%, 25% or 50%.
Option spacing: the gaps between answer options.
Rounding error: the difference between exact and rounded value.
Sanity check: a rough comparison to confirm the size of an answer.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: If the options are 10% apart, an estimate within 3% is enough. Choose the precision from the option spacing.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Round to two significant figures, use benchmark fractions, compute roughly, and then compare with the options.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Ratio
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Divide and round to a simple ratio

mainNarrative: Company A grew from 4,180 to 4,970. Round to 4,200 and 5,000: growth is 800 ÷ 4,200 ≈ 19%. The exact value is 18.9%.

For a share, round the total: the 2023 total is 4,970 + 3,890 + 6,010 + 3,540 + 2,430 ≈ 20,840. Company C is 6,010 ÷ 20,840 ≈ 29%. If the options are 25%, 29%, 33% and 38%, an estimate of "about 30%" picks 29%.
For a ratio, A : E in 2023 is 4,970 : 2,430, which is just over 2 : 1.
Use benchmarks: 15% of 2,430 is 10% (243) plus 5% (121.5) = 364.5, so a 15% rise gives about 2,795.
Check the answer against the data: a growth percentage cannot exceed the largest ratio of the new to old numbers minus one.

deepDiveAspects.title: Error budget
deepDiveAspects.content: Rounding each number to 2 significant figures typically gives an error under 3%; this is safe when options differ by 10% or more.

deepDiveAspects.title: When not to approximate
deepDiveAspects.content: If two options are within 2% of each other, calculate exactly.

solvedExamples.title: Rounding for growth
solvedExamples.question: Revenue rose from 4,180 to 4,970. Approximately what is the percentage growth?

solvedExamples.title: Ratio
solvedExamples.question: Revenue of A is 4,970 and of E is 2,430. Approximately what is the ratio A : E?

shortcutMethods.title: Round, benchmark, compare

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Round to two figures, use 10% and 5% benchmarks, estimate, and pick the option that is nearest.

rulesForApplication: Exact only if options are close.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rounding too early on close options

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Round both up or both down for ratios.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Discard options that are obviously too large or too small.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Estimate first, calculate only if needed.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Approximation is a skill: practise it daily.
